_comment: Pinned versions of the third-party tooling Aerie provisions with.
These are structural in the sense docs/ethos.md means it: identical for
every installation, so they belong in git rather than in per-repository
Actions variables. A second operator running this repo gets the same k3s
and the same Flux the author tested with, without being told what to type.
Site-specific values - domains, addresses, key material - stay as vars/
secrets, because those genuinely differ per install.
Bump these in a commit, deliberately, one line at a time. To try a bump
before merging it, dispatch the provisioning workflow from the branch
that carries it; every script also takes an explicit override parameter
for a by-hand run. Never point any of them at a 'latest' or 'stable'
channel - a moving pin makes a rebuilt node a different node.
Read by scripts/lib/AerieVersions.ps1.
Full k3s release tag, including the +k3sN build suffix, as passed to
INSTALL_K3S_VERSION. Deliberately one minor behind the stable channel:
k3s maintains four minor lines at once, and the ecosystem installed on
top of it (Longhorn, CloudNativePG, kube-vip) soaks against the older
ones first. Channel list: https://update.k3s.io/v1-release/channels
flux2 release tag. The CLI installed on the node and the controllers it
bootstraps are the same version, so this one pin covers both.
Releases: https://github.com/fluxcd/flux2/releases
AWS CLI v2 for Windows, installed on any runner that seeds the SSM
parameter tree (Provision 2). Note the URL is the *version-specific*
MSI, not https://awscli.amazonaws.com/AWSCLIV2.msi - that one is a
moving 'latest' pointer, so a hash pinned against it would break on
every upstream release. The versioned artifact is immutable, which is
what makes the hash below meaningful. AWS publishes no checksum file
for it, so - same as qemuImg - the hash is computed once from this
exact URL and re-derivable by anyone:
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 <the downloaded msi>
Bump all three fields together, and say in the commit message how the
new hash was obtained.
Treated as a floor, not an exact match: a runner already carrying a
*newer* aws.exe keeps it, with a warning. The pin exists so a bare
machine converges somewhere known, and AWS CLI v2 is backwards
compatible across minors - downgrading a shared runner (which other
workflows also use) would be a worse failure than running one release
ahead. Older or absent installs are brought up to this exact version.
Releases: https://github.com/aws/aws-cli/blob/v2/CHANGELOG.rst
qemu-img for Windows, used once per host to convert the vendor cloud
image from qcow2 to VHDX. Cloudbase publishes no checksum file, so the
hash below is pinned here instead - computed once from this exact URL,
and re-derivable by anyone:
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 <the downloaded zip>
If the URL 404s, check https://cloudbase.it/qemu-img-windows/, bump both
fields together, and say in the commit message how the new hash was
obtained. Bumping the URL without the hash is worse than no pin at all.
